comparing the renders with the concept

score 4/10: The ears stick up and out like a terrier's. The concept's defining feature is big floppy brown ears hanging flat down the sides of the head. The hinge angle signs are reversed.; The ears are too small (3x4) compared with the concept's long 3x5 ears, which reach down to the neck.; The tail flops sideways over the rear and hides behind the body. It should stand up and back, tan with a brown tip.
comparing the renders with the concept

score 3/10: The ears stick straight up like a rabbit's. The hinge angles have the wrong sign, so they lift the ears instead of letting them hang down the sides of the head. That is the main reason it doesn't read as a dog. The concept's ears are flat panels on the sides of the head, studs facing out, so they are now side-stud panels.; The tail droops down against the back. The angle of -60 on a child that extends toward +x swings it down; it should be +60 so the tail curls up with its brown tip.; The head is the same width as the body, so the whole model reads as one tall narrow column. In the concept the head is clearly wider and boxier than the body. The head is now 8 studs wide over a 6-stud body.
comparing the renders with the concept

score 5/10: The ears are the dog's signature feature, and they are too small. They are 3x4 studs, sit high on the head and curl like shells from the curved slopes. In the concept they are large flat brown flaps that hang from the top of the head down past the jaw to the shoulders.; The right ear's rows run downward, so its attach cell has to mirror the left ear's to make both ears hang down.; The tail is a short stub lying back along the body. The concept has a longer tail pointing up and back with a brown tip.
